claude.sample_unit: deliveries (births): 183,836 in South Carolina and 696,963 in Florida
models_evaluated: NYC postpartum hospital use LASSO logistic regression model (21 predictors)
Updated models (recalibrated intercept; re-estimated coefficients; plus driving distance and rurality)

links.outcome: Calibration of NYC-developed model applied to SC and FL populations
links.effect: Original NYC coefficients gave overestimated, extreme risk in new states; calibration slope 0.64 in SC and 0.63 in FL, while AUC stayed 0.68-0.69.
links.quote: Calibration slope was 0.64 in SC and 0.63 in FL, suggesting that predicted risks were more extreme compared to observed risk.

links.outcome: Calibration and AUC after local intercept recalibration and coefficient re-estimation
links.effect: Intercept update corrected calibration; re-estimating coefficients raised AUC to 0.69 (SC) and 0.70 (FL), with slight gains in subgroups.
links.quote: Model updating improved calibration in both states ( Figure ), with substantial improvement after adjusting model intercepts

links.outcome: Model performance when extended to new geographic populations, before and after updating
links.effect: NYC model overestimated risk in SC/FL but modest updating yielded well-calibrated models with AUC 0.69-0.70.
links.quote: Modest model updating, including recalibration of intercepts and re-estimation of coefficients, yielded well-calibrated models without requiring new predictors.

links.outcome: Performance across sites (states) of prediction model
links.effect: Discrimination was similar across SC (AUC 0.68) and FL (0.69) versus NYC 0.69, but calibration was poor in both states.
links.quote: The model achieved an AUC of 0.68 (95% CI 0.67 –0.68) and 0.69 (95% CI 0.68–0.69) in discriminating PHU among SC and FL births, respectively ( Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Model discrimination across racial/ethnic, Medicaid, and rural subgroups
links.effect: AUC was lower in Black (0.63-0.65), Medicaid (0.64-0.67), and rural (0.65-0.66) groups than overall (0.68-0.69) with the original model.
links.quote: AUC decreased when models were run separately among Black, Hispanic, Medicaid-insured, and rural residents.

links.outcome: Performance of the model in external, later-period, multi-state data versus development
links.effect: External validation showed similar AUC but overestimated absolute risk, so calibration was poor.
links.quote: However, calibration was poor and indicated systematic overprediction of PHU risk.

unlisted_practices: Testing whether adding hospital access indicators (driving distance, rurality) improves prediction; no meaningful change in calibration or discrimination

links.effect: Calibration slope was 0.64 in SC and 0.63 in FL, indicating overly extreme predicted risks.
links.quote: Calibration slope was 0.64 in SC and 0.63 in FL, suggesting that predicted risks were more extreme compared to observed risk.

links.quote: Updating model intercepts corrected calibration, and additionally re-estimating coefficients resulted in an AUC of 0.69 (95% CI 0.68-0.69) in SC and 0.70 (95% CI 0.70-0.71) in FL.

links.effect: Original AUC lower in subgroups: SC Black 0.63, Hispanic 0.65, Medicaid 0.64, rural 0.65; FL 0.65/0.68/0.67/0.66.

links.quote: Updating model intercepts corrected calibration, and additionally re-estimating coefficients resulted in an AUC of 0.69 (95% CI 0.68-0.69) in SC and 0.70 (95% CI 0.70-0.71) in FL.
